claims.text: What the image looks like Figure of 3 sign / rib notching → coarctation of the aorta
claims.quote: Figure of 3 sign / rib notching Coarctation of the aorta
claims.locator: Chest X-Ray (CXR), Pediatric / Congenital CXR Signs table

claims.text: Buzzword: figure of 3 / rib notching on CXR → coarctation of the aorta
claims.quote: Figure of 3 / rib notching CXR Coarctation of the aorta

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Bones / soft tissue: rib fractures, lytic lesions, rib notching, subQ air
claims.quote: B - Bones / soft tissue: rib fractures, lytic lesions, rib notching, subQ air, breast shadows.
claims.locator: Chest X-Ray (CXR), Reading Approach (RIPE technical adequacy → ABCDE-FGHI)

claims.text: Chest x-ray: a “3” sign in the upper left mediastinal shadow; heart size is normal unless heart failure supervenes
claims.quote: Chest x-ray shows coarctation as a “3” sign in the upper left mediastinal shadow. Heart size is normal unless heart failure supervenes.

claims.text: Dilated intercostal collateral arteries may erode the 3rd to 8th ribs, causing rib notching, seldom seen before age 5 years
claims.quote: Dilated intercostal collateral arteries may erode the 3rd to 8th ribs, causing rib notching, but this radiographic sign is seldom seen before age 5 years.

claims.text: Causes A localized narrowing of the lumen, typically in the proximal thoracic aorta just beyond the left subclavian artery, next to the opening of the ductus arteriosus
claims.quote: Coarctation of the aorta is a localized narrowing of the lumen, typically in the proximal thoracic aorta just beyond the left subclavian artery and adjacent to the opening of the ductus arteriosus.

claims.text: May occur alone or with other anomalies: bicuspid aortic valve, VSD, aortic stenosis, PDA, mitral valve disorders, intracerebral aneurysms
claims.quote: Coarctation may occur alone or with various other congenital anomalies (eg, bicuspid aortic valve, ventricular septal defect, aortic stenosis, patent ductus arteriosus, mitral valve disorders, intracerebral aneurysms).

claims.text: Occurs in 10 to 20% of patients with Turner syndrome
claims.quote: It occurs in 10 to 20% of patients with Turner syndrome.

claims.text: Symptoms Severe: can present in the neonatal period with acidosis, renal insufficiency and shock; mild: may not be apparent until an adolescent or adult is evaluated for hypertension or diminished femoral pulses
claims.quote: Severe coarctation can manifest in the neonatal period with acidosis, renal insufficiency, and shock, but mild coarctation may not be apparent until an adolescent or adult is evaluated for hypertension or diminished femoral pulses.

claims.text: Typically an upper-to-lower extremity blood pressure gradient and pulse amplitude differential, and a grade 2 to 3/6 ejection systolic murmur, sometimes loudest in the left interscapular area
claims.quote: There is typically a blood pressure gradient between upper and lower extremities, an easily distinguished amplitude differential between the upper and lower extremity pulses, and a grade 2 to 3/6 ejection systolic murmur, sometimes most prominent in the left interscapular area.

claims.text: As children age, subtle symptoms may appear (headache, chest pain, fatigue, leg claudication with activity); upper-extremity hypertension is often present
claims.quote: Subtle symptoms (eg, headache, chest pain, fatigue, and leg claudication during physical activities) may be present as children age. Upper-extremity hypertension is often present, but heart failure rarely develops after the neonatal period.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: surgical or balloon repair
claims.locator: Chest X-Ray (CXR), Pediatric / Congenital CXR Signs table

claims.text: Symptomatic neonates: prostaglandin E1 to reopen the constricted ductus arteriosus
claims.quote: For symptomatic neonates, infuse prostaglandin E1 to reopen the constricted ductus arteriosus.

claims.text: Correct surgically or by balloon angioplasty with or without stent placement
claims.quote: Correct coarctation surgically or using balloon angioplasty with or without stent placement.
